candidates.summary: We study outlier tokens in Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) for image generation. We show that this phenomenon appears in both the encoder and denoiser of modern Representation Autoencoder (RAE)-DiT pipelines: pretrained ViT encoders can produce outlier representations, and DiTs themselves can develop internal outlier tokens, especially in intermediate layers…

candidates.summary: Preference alignment has become a crucial component in enhancing the performance of Large Language Models (LLMs), yet its impact in Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) remains comparatively underexplored. In MLLMs, hallucination can occur not only by stating incorrect facts but also by producing responses that are inconsistent with the image content. candidates.title: Don't assume your final checkpoint is the best one to quantize
candidates.summary:
Don’t assume your final checkpoint is the best one to quantizeLate in pretraining, benchmarks can stay flat while 4-bit fragility quietly increases.

On the suites I could measure on one consumer GPU (Pythia scales, OLMo-2-1B, TinyLlama) we saw this pattern: on Pythia-160m the final checkpoint takes ~4× more Q4 damage than an equal-quality earlier one. It correlates with rank compression of the mean depth-update. On TinyLlama the effect is simply absent.
